detail.title: Nonreciprocal Coupling and Coarse-Grained Dissipation Bounds
detail.summary: Thermodynamic dissipation in nonequilibrium systems is intrinsically constrained by the resolution of the information-processing mechanism. While generalized TURs provide lower bounds on entropy production, finite-information reconstruction—specifically propagation delay and observer-relative bandwidth—further refines the effective dissipation cost. True predictive memory requires operational sufficiency, where state persistence is insufficient without corresponding reductions in future uncertainty.
detail.reason: Revising the project notebook to incorporate new operational constraints on information flow and finite-information reconstruction which challenge previous assumptions of infinite-resolution feedback.
